# Why does Isaac Lab fail to initialize when the IMU's target prim is just a transform with valid transform, but no RigidBodyAPI? What is the root cause and versioned handling?

> **Current answer:** In the original Isaac Lab v2.1.1/Isaac Sim 4.5.0 environment, IMU reads the pose, velocity, and center of mass (CoM) buffer of PhysX rigid bodies via create_rigid_body_view, so the target prim must have RigidBodyAPI; only a transform with only transform will fail initialization. Subsequent merged PR #3864 added Xform mounting and automatic parent-body discovery, with testing. Actual handling should first check if the installation version includes this PR: if yes, use the new behavior; if not, must align the target to an available rigid body or re-evaluate the fix. Cannot assume any version has the old behavior.

## Problem and symptoms

- Why does Isaac Lab fail to initialize when the IMU's target prim is just a transform with valid transform, but no RigidBodyAPI?
- ImuCfg initialization throws RuntimeError: Failed to find a RigidBodyAPI for the prim paths.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab v2.1.1; Isaac Sim 4.5.0; ergoCub; target prim=/ergoCub/root_link/torso_1/waist_imu_0; original implementation commit 77a6498.

## Priority diagnostics

- Check if the target prim has UsdPhysics.RigidBodyAPI; confirm data comes from PhysX rigid body buffer via calls to create_rigid_body_view, get_transforms, get_velocities, and get_coms in imu.py.

## Possible causes

- Old IMU implementation only read data from PhysX rigid body buffers, which were maintained by the physics engine; regular transforms do not have these data.

## Attempts

- The questioner modified the IMU to support Xform; subsequent official PR #3864 implements automatic parent-body discovery and adds testing.

## Effective fixes

- Use a version containing PR #3864 to make IMU point to Xform and automatically discover an available parent rigid body; old versions cannot assume any Xform can directly create a rigid body view.

## Result

- PR #3864 merged into isaac-sim/IsaacLab main on 2025-12-10, with description matching #3088, and the test added to confirm the fix is valid.
